Regulatory Agencies.content:
Roundups
27 August 2026
by Nick Paul Taylor
Euro Roundup: MHRA updates guidance on submitting safety reports for UK products
The Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) has updated its pharmacovigilance procedures guidance with new advice about periodic safety update reports (PSURs).
MHRA’s update centers on the European Union Reference Date (EURD) list. The EURD list is the European Medicines Agency’s comprehensive repository of individual and combined active substances contained in authorized medicinal products. First
published
in 2012, the list’s information includes the frequencies for submission of PSURs.
Despite Brexit, MHRA continues to require PSURs for UK products to be submitted according to the EURD list. The updated guidance addresses how marketing authorization holders (MAHs) can comply with that demand in a specific circumstance.
“If your active is removed from the EURD list you should continue with the PSUR frequency last presented in the EURD list unless you are informed otherwise,” MHRA said. “In order to support this, it is recommended that you retain a copy of the EURD list that last contained the entry for your active.”
EMA
updates
the EURD list each month based on new safety information, authorizations, and requests from MAHs. MHRA’s revised guidance clarifies that UK requirements for submitting PSURs are unaffected by the cessation of EMA requirements. A similar situation is already present within the EU, where some products assessed at a national level are excluded from the list but still subject to PSUR requirements.
MHRA Guidance
EDQM revises advice on electronic Certificate of Suitability applications
The European Directorate for the Quality of Medicines and HealthCare (EDQM) has revised its guidance on applying for a Certificate of Suitability to the monographs of the European Pharmacopoeia (CEP).
EDQM updated its advice on applying electronically for a CEP to reflect current requirements, specifically regarding the need to provide an electronic common technical document (eCTD) validation report. The directorate
began
requiring applicants to provide an eCTD validation report as part of eCTD submissions in November. EDQM introduced the requirement as part of a push to automate processes.
To help applicants comply with the requirement, EDQM updated its guidance on electronic submissions of CEP applications. The update, which EDQM made last week, describes how the eCTD validation report should be named. Other new information covers the right place to put the report in the CEP application and EDQM’s preferred format.
EDQM also clarified that changes to the content of module 3 of a CEP application should be described in module 1. Applicants should not highlight the content changes in module 3 itself. EDQM is encouraging applicants to consult the updated guidance to ensure they comply with the revised requirements when preparing CEP submissions.
EDQM Notice
Swissmedic enhances portal to eliminate need for temporary workaround
The Swiss Agency for Therapeutic Products (Swissmedic) has changed the software architecture for its portal to better support its evolving business requirements.
Through the changes, Swissmedic has created a new dedicated overview page that provides access to all currently valid establishment licenses. Users can select entries in the table to view the corresponding license details. Making the details available directly within the portal marks the end of the use of a temporary workaround, which required users to view the information through the partner overview.
Swissmedic is planning further improvements to the establishment license overview page. The next step is to provide historical establishment license data within the same overview and allow users to filter and select license records by status. The feature will be available in “the near future,” Swissmedic said.
The agency disclosed the changes alongside other updates to the portal. Swissmedic has changed the navigation structure to “improve future scaled usability needs” and added the option to temporarily change the display language of the portal.
Other changes lay the foundations for further updates. By moving to a new URL structure, Swissmedic has provided the basis for the addition of business domains, such as medicinal products, in the future.
Swissmedic Notice
NICE backs Lilly’s weekly insulin for UK use ahead of MHRA approval decision
The UK National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) has published final draft guidance recommending Eli Lilly’s weekly insulin for the treatment of type 2 diabetes.
NICE’s decision, which arrived before MHRA approval, requires the English health service to fund Lilly’s insulin efsitora alfa for type 2 diabetes. Healthcare professionals should use the least expensive of the suitable treatments, including insulin efsitora alfa and once- or twice-daily basal insulin. Assessments of expense should consider administration costs, dosages, price per dose, and commercial arrangements.
“The biggest cost saving from using insulin efsitora alfa comes from people needing less support to take their insulin. This is because insulin efsitora alfa is taken once a week rather than every day,” NICE said. “An average of one hour with a specialist district nurse for diabetes is assumed each time a person needs help taking insulin.”
NICE’s comparison suggests the overall cost of insulin efsitora alfa, which Lilly will sell as Onswik, may be the same or cheaper than once- or twice-daily basal insulin. While NICE has backed Onswik, MHRA has yet to approve the product for use in the UK.
Press Release
,
Draft Guidance
Turkish board probes impact of Teva’s patent practices on pharma competition
The Turkish Competition Board is investigating whether Teva Pharmaceutical tried to make it harder for competitors to enter a market.
In a preliminary inquiry, the board looked at whether Teva engaged in conduct intended to restrict competition from generic medicines. Potentially anticompetitive practices assessed by the board include “the strategic use of divisional patent procedures” and the creation of “a misleading impression before healthcare authorities regarding the efficacy and safety of competing products.”
The term “divisional patent procedures” describes splitting an initial application into multiple filings, for example to tackle concerns about single submissions claiming multiple inventions. Medicines for Europe, a trade group representing generic drugmakers, has
warned
that allowing unlimited filing of divisional patents opens the door to a widespread misuse of the system to artificially delay competition.
Going forward, the Turkish board will investigate Teva patent applications relating to a manufacturing process and dosage regimen. The board wants to know whether the patents, together with associated withdrawal practices, could restrict competition from generic medicines. Last year, Teva
appealed
an EU fine of €462.6 million ($539.1 million) related to claims it tried to delay competition to Copaxone.
Press Release
France’s ANSM enlists 14 drugmakers for pilot push to increase drug shelf lives
The French National Agency for Medicines and Health Products Safety (ANSM) has started a pilot project to extend the shelf life of 73 medicines.
Last year, ANSM called for applications from drugmakers that intended to file to increase the shelf life of a product in the next five years. The agency received responses from 14 drugmakers, including AstraZeneca, that will participate in the pilot project to increase the shelf lives of widely used medicines such as paracetamol.
Currently, the products have shelf lives of 12 to 48 months. The targeted shelf lives range from 24 to 60 months. Boiron aims to extend the shelf life of one product from 12 to 60 months. Almost two-thirds of the products will have shelf lives of 48 months or longer if the pilot achieves its targets. ANSM framed the project to reduce waste and the environmental impact of drug production and disposal.

Regulatory Agencies.url_match_title: Cuisinart Wire Grill Brush Recall Grows; Wire Bristle Injuries Tripled Despite Safety Warnings - Tech Times
Regulatory Agencies.content:
By
Devin Culbertson
Published: Aug 27 2026, 3:24 PM EDT
Share on Facebook
Share on Twitter
Share on LinkedIn
Share on Reddit
Share on Flipboard
Share on Pocket
Cuisinart.com
If you own a Cuisinart wire bristle grill brush, the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission has announced today that it qualifies for a free refund — whether or not the model number is on any previous recall list. Conair, the parent company of Cuisinart, has expanded its Cuisinart wire bristle grill brush recall from roughly 1.72 million to more than 3.6 million total units, adding approximately 1.9 million brushes to the initial action issued last month. The expansion brings the total number of wire bristle grill brushes recalled across three brands in 2026 alone — Weber, Nexgrill, and now Cuisinart — to approximately 17 million units, as confirmed by
the CPSC's official recall announcement
.
That number reveals something the individual recall announcements obscured: this is not a series of isolated product defects. It is a systemic failure of an entire product category — and it has been playing out for more than two decades with no mandatory federal safety standard to stop it.
What the Expansion Covers
Today's action adds approximately 1,905,805 brushes to the 1,719,995 units already recalled on July 2, 2026, for a combined total of about 3,625,800 Cuisinart wire bristle grill brushes. The hazard in every case is the same: small metal wire bristles detach from the brush head during normal use, stick to grill grates or food, and can be swallowed by anyone who eats food cooked on that grill, posing a risk of serious internal injuries that may require surgery. The full scope of the expanded Cuisinart recall is detailed on CPSC.gov.
The expansion adds models sold under the Cuisinart brand from June 2009 through March 2026, including the Dual Grip Grill Brush (CGWM-024), the 18-inch Bamboo Cleaning Grill Brush (CGWM-059), the Grill Dozer Steam Cleaning Tool (FCB-501), the 18 Piece Wooden Handle Grill Set (CGS-W18), the Comfort Grill Cleaning Brush (CCB-134), the Cross Action Grill Cleaning Brush (CB-395), and the Triple Threat Grill Brush (CCB-3001), among others. In addition, Conair has specified that all Cuisinart wire bristle grill brushes sold prior to 2020 are included in the recall, even if the model number does not appear on the published list.
These brushes were sold at Walmart, Burlington, TJ Maxx, and Ross, and online through Amazon and Cuisinart.com, for between $8 and $20. Conair is aware of at least 54 reports and consumer reviews in which wire bristles detached from the brushes, including three cases requiring surgical extraction from the digestive tract.
Why the Bristle Is So Dangerous
The hazard is not visible to the naked eye, and that invisibility is the key reason it has injured thousands of people over more than two decades. Wire bristles on grill brushes are manufactured as looped tufts of metal wire — typically thin-gauge stainless steel — twisted and crimped around an aluminum coil at the brush head. Unlike designs in which bristles are chemically bonded or molded into the head material, this crimp-and-coil attachment method degrades with repeated exposure to high grill temperatures (often exceeding 400°F/204°C) and the mechanical stress of scrubbing. Over time, individual wires fatigue, loosen, and separate. Once detached, a bristle — typically 16 to 17 millimeters (roughly two-thirds of an inch) long and just over a millimeter wide — has enough curvature and surface tension to embed itself in the surface of a hamburger patty or other soft protein during cooking.
The bristle then goes onto the plate, and into the mouth, entirely undetected.
What makes the injury particularly dangerous is how hard it is to diagnose afterward. A
standard lateral neck X-ray detects
ingested metal bristles only about 50% of the time, according to published case reports. Dr. Mark Prince, chair of the Department of Otolaryngology at Michigan Medicine, put it plainly after treating a patient whose bristle had been missed on initial imaging: bristles from grill cleaning brushes "are often very difficult to identify visually or by radiology exams, often resulting in the need for multiple examinations until someone sorts out what is happening." CT imaging is the most reliable diagnostic tool, but even reaching a CT requires a clinician to suspect the ingestion — a difficult leap when the injury can present as generic throat soreness, difficulty swallowing, or abdominal pain that mimics a range of common conditions.
Delayed diagnosis is common. Published case series document
presentations up to 25 days
after ingestion, by which point abscesses had begun forming. Bowel perforation — the worst-case outcome — requires emergency surgery, either laparoscopic or open, as documented in
peer-reviewed surgical case reports
.
Dr. Meghan Martin, a pediatric emergency physician at Johns Hopkins All Children's Hospital in Florida, has treated multiple children for this injury and
issued a public warning
: "Do not use grill brushes with metal wires."
How Many Americans Have Been Hurt
The number of people injured by wire grill brush bristles nationally is substantially larger than the figures attached to any individual recall. A
2016 epidemiology study
published in Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery estimated approximately 1,698 emergency department visits attributable to wire bristle grill brush injuries between 2002 and 2014.
A more recent study — published in the International Journal of Pediatric Otorhinolaryngology in March 2026, by researchers at UPMC Children's Hospital of Pittsburgh — found the problem accelerated significantly in the following decade. The
research tallied approximately 3,739 reported injuries
from 2015 through 2023, with the oropharynx (the region of the throat behind the mouth) as the most common injury site, accounting for 40% of cases. Nearly one in four patients — about 24% — required hospital admission rather than being treated and released from the emergency department. The researchers concluded that
awareness campaigns over the preceding decade
had not meaningfully reduced the injury rate.
The 2026 Recall Wave: Three Brands, 17 Million Brushes
Today's Cuisinart expansion is the fourth major development in a recall wave that began at the end of February. On February 26, 2026,
the CPSC announced that Weber-Stephen Products
had recalled more than 3.2 million metal wire bristle grill brushes sold under six model numbers at Lowe's, Home Depot, Ace Hardware, Target, Amazon, and Weber.com between 2011 and 2026 for between $10 and $17. Weber reported at least 38 incident reports, including four consumers who required medical treatment.
Less than a month later, on March 26, 2026, the CPSC announced an even larger action: Nexgrill Industries had recalled more than 10.2 million metal wire bristle grill brushes sold exclusively at Home Depot and homedepot.com between 2015 and 2026 for between $5 and $15. Nexgrill reported at least 68 incident reports, including five consumers who needed medical treatment. CPSC Chair Peter Feldman described that recall as driven by
a dangerous design defect
"that allows metal bristles to detach and be swallowed without detection" and explicitly called for consumers to switch to non-wire alternatives.
Conair's initial Cuisinart recall on July 2, 2026 then added another 1.72 million units. Today's expansion adds nearly 1.9 million more. The running total across all three brands: approximately 17 million recalled units in a single year.
No US Safety Standard Exists
What allowed 17 million wire bristle grill brushes to reach American consumers over more than a decade with a documented, recurring, and well-published hazard? The short answer is that the United States had no mandatory safety standard for wire grill brushes — and still does not.
The CPSC formally requested in May 2024 that ASTM International — the body that writes voluntary safety standards for thousands of consumer product categories — develop a new standard specifically for grill brushes, after reviewing more than 100 injury reports.
ASTM member Jason Fields
, who chairs the resulting subcommittee (F15.04), said the standard would "specifically cover concerns about bristles detaching during use and posing ingestion hazards to consumers." The subcommittee held its first meeting in October 2024.
As of May 2026 — when the CPSC published its FY2025 Annual Voluntary Standards Tracking and Reporting report — the standard had not been finalized.
Legal analyses of the recall wave
confirm that staff had conducted product testing, but the development of specific requirements was still ongoing.
Canada, by contrast, has had a voluntary safety standard from the Canadian Standards Association in place since 2019, establishing minimum bristle retention strength requirements — essentially a pull-force test ensuring bristles cannot be detached below a specified force threshold — along with mandatory labeling requirements.
That standard was created
after multiple reports of Canadians ingesting wire bristles from barbecue brushes. The US had no equivalent.
The implication for consumers who own wire grill brushes from brands other than Cuisinart, Weber, or Nexgrill: their brushes share the same fundamental crimped-wire attachment design and carry the same structural risk, because no mandatory US standard requires any wire grill brush to pass a minimum bristle retention test.
Legal Consequences Are Already Underway
The recall wave has triggered civil litigation. On March 9, 2026, plaintiffs Richard Malmstein and Geoffrey vonMaucher
filed a federal class action lawsuit
against Weber-Stephen Products in Illinois federal court, alleging that Weber sold brushes known to shed bristles during normal use while marketing materials emphasized durability without adequate safety warnings. Multiple plaintiff law firms have since opened intake for claims against Weber, Nexgrill, and Cuisinart from consumers who sustained bristle-related injuries. Product liability claims in this category typically assert design defect — arguing that the wire-in-coil attachment method is inherently unsafe for its intended use, affecting every unit manufactured, not just a defective batch.
This is also not the first time Conair has faced a "metal in food" recall under the Cuisinart brand name. In 2016,
Conair recalled approximately 8 million
Cuisinart food processors because riveted blades were cracking and shedding metal pieces into processed food.
What to Do Right Now
Stop using the brush immediately.
If you own any Cuisinart wire bristle grill brush — regardless of model number, if it has wire bristles and was purchased before March 2026 — stop using it. Consumers are not required to verify the model number; Conair has specified that all Cuisinart wire bristle grill brushes sold prior to 2020 are included in the recall.
Claim your refund or credit.
Two remedies are available:
Full cash refund: contact Conair and discard the brush.
Cuisinart.com store credit: receive the full refund amount plus an additional 20% credit to use on Cuisinart.com.
Contact Conair toll-free at
888-520-1304
, Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 6 p.m. ET, or visit recallrtr.com/grillbrushes or cuisinart.com and click "Product Recalls" at the bottom of the page.
Replace with a safer alternative.
Both the CPSC and the manufacturers themselves recommend alternatives: nylon-bristle brushes (Weber's own remedy is a nylon replacement), brass-bristle brushes, bristle-free coil brushes, or wooden scrapers. There is no reason to continue using a wire bristle brush of any brand — not just a recalled model.
Seek medical attention if needed.
If you have recently eaten food cooked on a grill cleaned with a wire brush and are experiencing throat soreness, difficulty swallowing, a globus sensation (feeling of something stuck in the throat), or abdominal pain, see a physician and mention the grill brush. Do not assume the symptom will resolve on its own. Alert the physician that a standard X-ray may not reveal the bristle — a CT scan is more reliable, and endoscopy may be required for removal.
How Does a Bristle Injure Someone?
A wire bristle detached from a grill brush is essentially a thin metal needle, typically 16 to 17 millimeters (roughly two-thirds of an inch) long. When it adheres invisibly to the surface of a hamburger or other grilled food and is swallowed, it can puncture the soft tissue of the mouth, throat, esophagus, or intestines at any point along the digestive tract. At the oropharynx — the most common injury site, accounting for 40% of documented cases — the bristle may lodge in the tonsil tissue and begin causing an abscess if not removed. Further down the digestive tract, a lodged bristle can perforate the stomach or intestinal wall, producing acute abdominal pain, internal bleeding, and in severe cases, sepsis requiring emergency surgery. The injury is categorically difficult to connect to a grill brush: the symptom onset may be delayed by hours or days after ingestion, the bristle is too small to feel passing through the throat, and there is no dramatic choking event to alert the patient.
Frequently Asked Questions
How do I know if my Cuisinart grill brush is recalled?
If your Cuisinart grill brush has wire metal bristles — the thin, stiff metal wires that look like steel wool stretched over a scrubbing head — it is almost certainly covered by the recall. Conair has specified that all Cuisinart wire bristle grill brushes sold prior to 2020 are included regardless of model number, and specific models sold through March 2026 are also included. Check the list of model numbers (CCB-100, CCB-4125, CCB-5014, CCB-6450, CCB-8012, CCB-4114, CCB-W2, CSBS-777, CGWM-024, CGWM-059, FCB-501, CGS-W18, CCB-134, CB-395, CCB-3001, and others) at cpsc.gov or cuisinart.com, or simply call Conair at 888-520-1304 to confirm. When in doubt: if it has wire bristles and a Cuisinart label, treat it as recalled.
Why can't a doctor find an ingested grill brush bristle on an X-ray?
A metal wire bristle is about the thickness of a piece of thread. On a standard lateral neck radiograph, it appears only about half the time, according to published case reports — its small size, thinness, and slight curvature make it easy to miss against the surrounding tissue structures. CT imaging is the most reliable diagnostic tool. If you suspect bristle ingestion, explicitly ask the treating physician for a CT scan rather than relying on X-ray alone, and be sure to mention the grill brush — without that history, a physician may not think to look for a metal foreign body.
What is the safest grill brush alternative to wire bristles?
Nylon-bristle brushes, brass-bristle brushes (softer than steel and less prone to shedding), bristle-free coil brushes (a stainless steel coil rather than individual wires), and wooden scrapers are all established alternatives. Weber is replacing recalled brushes with a nylon-bristle model. For cast iron grates, steam-cleaning brushes — which use a damp pad and heat to loosen residue — also avoid the bristle problem entirely. Any of these alternatives eliminates the specific ingestion risk associated with metal wire bristles.
Why hasn't the government set a mandatory safety standard for wire grill brushes?
The US still does not have a mandatory safety standard for wire grill brushes. The CPSC formally asked ASTM International to develop a voluntary standard in May 2024, after reviewing more than 100 injury reports — and ASTM formed a dedicated subcommittee (F15.04) for that purpose. But as of May 2026, the standard had not been finalized. Canada established its own voluntary standard in 2019, requiring minimum bristle retention strength testing and labeling. Until the US adopts a mandatory standard requiring wire grill brushes to pass minimum bristle retention tests, any wire bristle brush on the US market — recalled brand or otherwise — is sold without an independently verified safety specification.

Regulatory Agencies.content:
Sen. Bill Cassidy, R-La., talks with reporters in the Capitol this month. (
Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call
)
By
Ariel Cohen
Posted August 27, 2026 at 9:00am
Facebook
Twitter
Email
Reddit
Sen. Bill Cassidy is accusing abortion pill manufacturers of not meeting their legal responsibilities to ensure compliance with Food and Drug Administration safety regulations, especially when pills are sold online through third-party providers.
A report issued Thursday by Cassidy, chair of the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee, follows the panel’s monthslong investigation into the three mifepristone manufacturers: Danco Laboratories, GenBioPro and Evita Solutions.
The report calls on legal and regulatory authorities to take action.
Republicans have rallied around safety concerns of medication abortion since the Biden administration expanded mail-order access to the pill during the COVID-19 pandemic. Conservatives also argue mailing pills across state lines undermines state abortion restrictions.
Cassidy, who is leaving Congress in January, accuses abortion pill makers of allowing third-party retailers to sell the drugs without oversight and failing to report non-fatal adverse events. He says that the Department of Justice should explore legal avenues to address willful noncompliance with safety requirements and that the FDA should take immediate action to reestablish an in-person dispensing requirement for mifepristone.
“We are seeing that the explosion in online sales of chemical abortion drugs has opened the door to coercion and abuse of women,” Cassidy said in a statement.
Cassidy has not yet announced any coming legislative action or hearings on the topic.
The report uses the example of the website Aid Access, which allows individuals to order mifepristone online without an in-person patient-provider relationship. This sort of telehealth prescribing is allowed under the Biden-era rules. The website was launched by a physician and abortion-rights activist.
But Cassidy’s report says it is unclear who is providing the drug when ordered online and whether those parties are certified in the FDA’s Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy program. The Aid Access website also advertises prescribing mifepristone through 14 weeks of pregnancy — beyond the 10-week limit set by the FDA.
Cassidy says that Danco and GenBioPro told his committee throughout its investigation that the companies have no role in ensuring that health care providers that prescribe mifepristone maintain compliance with FDA requirements. Both Danco and GenBioPro have links on their websites to Aid Access.
The companies vigorously defended their records on safety.
GenBioPro said in a statement that it is “deeply committed to complying with all regulatory frameworks that govern our business and disputes any suggestion to the contrary. Furthermore, the safety and efficacy of mifepristone is backed by more than a quarter century of rigorous scientific research, regulatory review, and real-world use, and remains unchanged.”
A Danco spokesperson accused the committee of cherry picking details to suggest that mifepristone makers have been negligent, and said the report reflects a lack of understanding about FDA regulatory processes.
The committee report also notes that since the Obama administration removed a requirement that providers report non-fatal adverse events to mifepristone makers, very few incidents have been reported.
Drugmakers and congressional Democrats have pointed to that scarcity of non-fatal adverse events as evidence of its safety. For example, from 2000 to the 2016 change, Danco had reported roughly 4,000 non-fatal adverse events related to mifepristone, but the company has only reported 150 non-fatal adverse events in the last 10 years, the report says.
Court action
Meanwhile, a pending court case in which Louisiana is suing the FDA could determine the availability of mail and telehealth abortion pills nationwide. The Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals is scheduled to hear oral arguments on Sept. 9.
The Supreme Court intervened in the case earlier this year, granting an emergency request from abortion drug makers to preserve telemedicine access to medication abortion while the case continues.
The abortion drug has been available in the U.S. for 25 years, but became more widely accessible in 2021 when the Biden administration lifted the in-person dispensing requirement. By 2023, it accounted for 63 percent of all abortions in the U.S, according to the Guttmacher Institute, a research and policy organization focused on sexual and reproductive rights and health.
Democrats argue that medication abortion has undergone rigorous FDA scrutiny and has been used safely for 25 years by over 7 million women. They also say that allowing medication abortion via telehealth and mail delivery reduces unnecessary burdens on care, especially for patients in rural areas or living in states with strict abortion bans.
“Preserving evidence-based access to mifepristone, including when dispensed by mail or retail pharmacy, is necessary to mitigate the imminent harm facing members of the public,” more than 250 House and Senate Democrats wrote in an amicus brief to the Supreme Court regarding mifepristone access.
Meanwhile, the FDA is working on an internal review of the drug’s safety amid political pressure from anti-abortion groups, after having defended its approval for years before President Donald Trump was elected. Cassidy has accused the FDA of “dragging its feet” on the review of the safety of the abortion drug.
The agency did not respond to requests for comment on the status of this review.

Regulatory Agencies.url_match_title: FDA approves Revolution Medicines’ first in class targeted therapy for metastatic pancreatic cancer - PMLiVE
Regulatory Agencies.content:
The US FDA has approved Revolution Medicines’ Rasonque (daraxonrasib), a RAS inhibitor for the most common form of pancreatic cancer – delivering a new treatment option to patients with advanced pancreatic cancer months ahead of schedule.
Rasonque, a tablet taken once daily, targets multiple forms of a protein called RAS, a key driver of tumour growth in most patients with pancreatic adenocarcinoma, which arises from cells lining the ducts of the pancreas.
“Today’s approval provides a critical new option for patients facing an extraordinarily difficult and historically hard-to-treat cancer,” said Acting FDA Commissioner Kyle Diamantas.
The approval is for the treatment of adults with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma who have received at least one prior systemic therapy or are not candidates for multiagent systemic therapy.
Approximately 90-95% of the 67,000 new cases of pancreatic cancer diagnosed in the US each year are pancreatic adenocarcinoma, according to the National Cancer Institute. Despite representing roughly 3.2% of all cancer diagnoses, pancreatic adenocarcinoma accounts for a disproportionately high share of cancer deaths, owing to its typically late detection, aggressive disease course and historically limited treatment options.
In a randomised, open-label, multicentre clinical trial involving 500 adults with previously treated metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma, Rasonque improved median overall survival to 13.2 months compared to 6.7 months for standard chemotherapy.
“This drug showed unprecedented results in an area of high unmet need,” said Angelo de Claro, director of the FDA’s Oncology Center of Excellence.
The FDA granted Rasonque Breakthrough Therapy and Orphan Drug designations. Rasonque received Priority Review for this indication. The application was also reviewed under the Commissioner’s National Priority Voucher pilot programme, which is intended to help accelerate the review of therapies that address national public health priorities.
In May, the FDA issued a ‘safe to proceed’ letter allowing the sponsor to initiate an expanded access treatment protocol for Rasonque, enabling patient access to the investigational drug prior to approval under applicable FDA regulations.
The most common side effects of the drug are rash, diarrhea, stomatitis (inflammation of the mouth’s mucus membranes), nausea, fatigue, vomiting, abdominal pain, oedema, decreased appetite and haemorrhage.

SL Science (NASDAQ: SLBT)
reported that JY BioMed, its GDT platform licensor and IP holder, has filed a new U.S. FDA Drug Master File (DMF No. 044612) covering exosomes derived from Gamma Delta T (GDT) cells. This adds to an existing DMF on GDT cells and extends FDA-filed manufacturing and quality documentation across both the cellular and cell-free exosome formats of the same core technology.
According to SL Science, DMFs centralize confidential chemistry, manufacturing and controls (CMC) data that downstream regulatory submissions can reference, potentially reducing CMC-related bottlenecks for future programs. The company highlights published preclinical and independent studies indicating that GDT-derived exosomes can trigger tumor cell death, stimulate immune responses, act synergistically with radiotherapy, remain active in immunosuppressive tumor environments, and cross the blood-brain barrier, which it views as particularly relevant to its focus on glioblastoma and other brain cancers.

"highlighted the filing of a new Drug Master File (DMF) with the U.S. Food"
A drug master file (DMF) is a confidential technical dossier submitted to regulators that describes the detailed chemistry, manufacturing and quality controls for an active drug ingredient or key component. Think of it as a supplier’s locked recipe and factory blueprint that regulators can inspect without the buyer revealing trade secrets. For investors, a DMF matters because it supports product approvals, protects supply-chain know‑how, and can speed regulatory review or signal manufacturing readiness.
chemistry, manufacturing, and controls
regulatory
"confidential chemistry, manufacturing, and controls (CMC) data"
Chemistry, manufacturing, and controls (CMC) is the detailed documentation of how a drug or medical product is made, tested, and kept consistent — like a recipe, factory checklist, and quality-control plan combined. Investors care because strong CMC means regulators are more likely to approve the product and the company can reliably scale production, while weak or incomplete CMC raises the risk of approval delays, production problems, extra costs, or recalls.
blood-brain barrier
medical
"delivering therapies across the blood-brain barrier"
A protective barrier of tightly packed cells and supporting tissue that controls what substances in the blood can enter the brain, acting like a security checkpoint that keeps out most pathogens and many drugs while allowing essential nutrients through. For investors, the barrier matters because whether a therapy can cross or safely bypass it often determines clinical success, regulatory approval and commercial potential for treatments of brain disorders.
extracellular vesicles
medical
"Unlike larger cells, extracellular vesicles such as exosomes"
Extracellular vesicles are tiny, cell-made particles—think microscopic bubbles—that carry proteins, genetic material and signals between cells. Investors care because these vesicles can be used as disease markers, drug-delivery vehicles, or therapeutic products; that creates opportunities and risks around clinical validation, manufacturing scale-up, intellectual property and regulatory approval that can materially affect the value of biotech and diagnostics companies.

Regulatory Agencies.url_match_title: FDA Nods Lilly-Roche's Alzheimer's Blood Test: Healthcare ETFs to Track Now - The Globe and Mail
Regulatory Agencies.content:
In a significant development for Alzheimer's diagnostics, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has recently granted clearance to the Elecsys pTau217 blood test, developed jointly by healthcare giants
Eli Lilly
LLY
and
Roche
RHHBY
. The test is designed to identify amyloid-beta pathology in individuals aged 55 and older exhibiting signs of cognitive decline, supporting both rule-in and rule-out assessments in primary and specialty care settings.
Notably, it is the first and only FDA-cleared single-biomarker blood test to offer this dual capability using one validated clinical cutoff.
This regulatory milestone comes against a backdrop of a mounting health crisis, with an estimated 7.4 million Americans aged 65 and older currently living with clinical Alzheimer's dementia, a figure projected to nearly double to 13.8 million by 2060 (as per
NIH data
).
With the long-term national care costs for people living with dementia
projected
to reach $409 billion by the end of this year, the FDA's green light for a more accessible, blood-based diagnostic tool thrusts both Eli Lilly and Roche, and by extension the healthcare exchange-traded funds (ETFs) that hold significant positions in these pharmaceutical giants, into the global investment spotlight.
But before identifying those particular ETFs, it is important to understand the commercial value of Alzheimer’s diagnostics and therapies and, ultimately, why sector-focused ETFs offer compelling portfolio exposure to this expanding market.
Booming Market for Alzheimer's Treatments
The economic landscape surrounding early detection and treatment of Alzheimer's represents one of the largest growth opportunities in modern biopharmaceuticals. To this end, it is imperative to mention that health and long-term care costs for American people living with dementia are projected to reach nearly $1 trillion in 2050.
With Alzheimer's disease being the leading cause of dementia, diagnostic tools like the Elecsys pTau217 getting regulatory approval should exponentially expand the eligible pool of patients for disease-modifying therapies (DMTs). Consequently, this should boost LLY and RHHBY’s revenue growth opportunities, with the global Alzheimer's DMT market projected to surge to $13.1 billion by the end of 2030 (as per
BCC Research data
).
Recognizing the growth potential of the Alzheimer’s DMT market, Eli Lilly and Roche, along with other pharmaceutical giants, are also funneling significant capital into this space. For instance,
AbbVie
ABBV
completed its acquisition of Aliada Therapeutics in late 2024 for $1.4 billion, gaining access to ALIA-1758, an investigational anti-pyroglutamate amyloid beta antibody currently in Phase 1 trials.
Biogen
BIIB
is conducting advanced research to support earlier diagnosis through blood-based biomarkers and investigating therapies directed at key drivers of Alzheimer’s disease biology, including amyloid and tau. Its Lecanemab anti-amyloid antibody, co-developed with Eisai, has recently expanded to include at-home administration options via subcutaneous autoinjector formulations for early-stage Alzheimer's patients.
Pharma giant
Novartis
NVS
is evaluating VHB937, a TREM2-targeting candidate currently in Phase 2 clinical trials for early Alzheimer's disease. The company has also entered into a massive licensing and collaboration agreement worth up to $1.7 billion with SciNeuro Pharmaceuticals to develop a next-generation, amyloid-beta-targeting antibody program.
Eli Lilly is independently conducting Phase 3 clinical trials for the efficacy of its donanemab in participants with preclinical Alzheimer's Disease. Notably, donanemab is an FDA-approved monoclonal antibody, designed to clear brain amyloid plaques in early symptomatic Alzheimer's patients.
Why Healthcare ETFs Offer a Strategic Investment Approach
For investors looking to gain exposure to the potential upside from the Alzheimer’s treatment market, healthcare ETFs present a compelling option.
Investing directly in individual biotech or pharmaceutical equities carries inherent concentration risk, as clinical trials can produce mixed efficacy results, regulatory delays, or patent disputes.
Instead, by investing in a healthcare ETF that counts the aforementioned stocks among its top holdings, investors can position themselves to benefit from the collective progress these companies are making in Alzheimer's diagnostics and therapeutics.
Healthcare ETFs to Track
Considering the aforementioned discussion, investors interested in capitalizing on the growth potential of Alzheimer’s treatment can add the following ETFs to their watchlist and invest once they seem fit:
State Street Health Care Select Sector SPDR ETF
XLV
This fund, with assets under management (AUM) worth $44.57 billion, offers exposure to 60 companies in the pharmaceuticals; health care equipment and supplies; health care providers and services; biotechnology; life sciences tools and services; and health care technology industries. Of these, LLY holds the first spot with 15.43% weightage, while ABBV holds the third spot with 7.42% weightage.
XLV has rallied 26.7% over the past year and charges 8 basis points (bps) in fees.
iShares Global Healthcare ETF
IXJ
This fund, with net assets worth $4.38 billion, offers exposure to 110 pharmaceutical, biotech, and medical device companies worldwide. Of these, LLY holds the first spot with 10.33% weightage, while ABBV holds the third spot with 4.97% weightage. RHHBY holds the fifth position in this fund with 3.90% weightage, while NVS holds the seventh spot with 3.49% weightage. BIIB holds 0.39% of this fund’s assets.
IXJ has gained 21.4% over the past year and charges 38 bps in fees.
VanEck Pharmaceutical ETF
PPH
This fund, with net assets worth $1.06 billion, offers exposure to 26 companies involved in pharmaceuticals, including research and development, as well as the production, marketing and sale of pharmaceuticals. Of these, LLY holds the first spot with 19.32% weightage, while NVS holds the third spot with 10.07% weightage. ABBV holds the eighth position in this fund with 4.49% weightage.
PPH has soared 30.4% over the past year and charges 36 bps in fees.
iShares Neuroscience and Healthcare ETF
IBRN
This fund, with net assets worth $8 million, offers exposure to 68 global companies advancing research and treatment of neurological disorders. Of these, Praxis Precision Medicines holds the first spot with 5.31% weightage, while BIIB holds the ninth position with 4.14% weightage.
IBRN has surged 60.6% over the past year and charges 47 bps in fees.

Regulatory Agencies.content:
GSK plc (ISIN GB0009252882) betreibt moderne Pharmaanlagen mit Laboren und Produktionshallen in der Abenddämmerung, Illustration mit AI erstellt.
GSK (ISIN GB0009252882) stock was quoted around the mid-$50 range in late August 2026, with one recent close at $51.43 on August 26, 2026, and a modest intraday pre-market quote of $51.28 reported the following morning, underscoring a steady valuation despite mixed daily moves. This trading range comes as the company highlights a fresh regulatory milestone for its HIV franchise in the United States.
Share price holds in low $50s
Recent market data show GSK American depositary shares trading close to $51.50, with a documented prior close of $51.43 on August 26, 2026, followed by a small pre-market gain to $51.28 reported on August 27, 2026. Over recent sessions, the stock has oscillated within the low-to-mid $50 band, with a separate late July 2026 snapshot capturing a close of $51.97 on July 28, 2026, after a daily increase of 3.48 percent and a subsequent move to $53.78 on July 29, 2026, where the shares slipped 1.17 percent from the prior day.
This price pattern positions GSK shares somewhat below their late July 2026 high of $55.79 recorded as the intraday peak on July 28, 2026, indicating a modest pullback from that level while still preserving gains relative to earlier in the year. Market data from late August 2026 also show the company with a market capitalization above $100 billion, including readings of $105.11 billion for July 27, 2026, and $108.77 billion for July 28, 2026, highlighting the scale at which small percentage price changes can translate into multi-billion-dollar swings in equity value.
Regulatory boost from Tivicay approval
Against this price backdrop, GSK received a meaningful regulatory boost through its HIV-focused subsidiary ViiV Healthcare, which secured US Food and Drug Administration approval for Tivicay PD to treat young children living with HIV. According to a late August 2026 update on the decision, the approval extends Tivicay PD to younger pediatric populations who previously had limited treatment options, reinforcing the durability of the company’s HIV portfolio as a cash-generating pillar within its pharmaceuticals segment.
The same update noted that GSK shares closed at $51.43 on August 26, 2026, down 1.23 percent on the day, before edging up to $51.28 in pre-market trading, suggesting that investors are still calibrating the long-term financial impact of the expanded label rather than reacting with a sharp short-term re-rating. Because the HIV business already contributes materially to group revenue and profit, incremental indications such as this one often build value over several years through sustained prescription volumes rather than immediate step-changes in quarterly results.
From an investor perspective, the Tivicay PD decision supports the broader narrative that GSK is seeking to offset historical patent expiries and litigation-related uncertainties by leaning on vaccines and specialty medicines. The approval is particularly important for maintaining competitive positioning in HIV, a therapeutic area in which long-acting regimens and convenient pediatric formulations can differentiate products and support pricing power, with the potential to underpin both revenue stability and margin resilience over the medium term.
Earnings context and recent trading activity
In the absence of a same-day earnings release, recent insider-related disclosures help frame sentiment. A late August 2026 report highlighted an executive acquisition of notional American depositary shares at a price of $51.78 per ADS executed on August 24, 2026, signaling internal confidence at a level close to where the stock continued to trade through August 26, 2026. That transaction took place on the New York Stock Exchange and, while modest in volume, provides a tangible reference point for how company leadership values the shares in the current environment.
Short-term market data underline that GSK’s valuation remains anchored in a range where daily moves of 1 to 3 percent have translated into shifts of several billion dollars in market capitalization over the second half of July 2026. For instance, the increase from a close of $51.38 on July 27, 2026, to $51.97 on July 28, 2026, coincided with an expansion in reported market value from $105.11 billion to $108.77 billion, a change of $3.66 billion in equity capitalization on a sub-2 percent share-price improvement. This sensitivity to modest price changes is a salient consideration for investors evaluating how news on pipeline assets or legal outcomes can ripple through the company’s market value.
While the latest full quarterly figures are not detailed in these late August 2026 sources, GSK’s recent communications have emphasized a strategic focus on vaccines, HIV, respiratory, and immunology therapies as growth drivers following its earlier consumer-healthcare separation. Historically, the company’s annual and interim results have underscored the importance of recurring vaccine and HIV revenues in supporting dividend capacity and funding ongoing research and development, and the Tivicay PD approval fits neatly into that pattern by targeting patient segments that can sustain long-duration treatment courses.
HIV franchise and Tivicay PD’s role
Within GSK’s portfolio, Tivicay and its pediatric formulation Tivicay PD form a cornerstone of the antiretroviral lineup that underpins the HIV franchise’s contribution to group sales. The new US approval for younger children, confirmed in late August 2026, extends the reach of this family of products and allows clinicians to dose pediatric patients more precisely, with weight-based regimens tailored to small children who need flexible, dispersible tablets.
This development complements existing adult and adolescent indications and may help protect market share as competitors also seek label expansions in pediatric HIV. For GSK, maintaining a broad and up-to-date label for Tivicay PD is strategically important, because pediatric treatment often involves long-term therapy that starts early in life and continues for many years, providing a recurring revenue stream that can smooth fluctuations elsewhere in the portfolio.
The company has previously indicated that it views HIV and specialty medicines as key areas where innovation can command premium pricing and support margins above those obtainable in more commoditized primary-care markets. By gaining regulatory clearance for an expanded Tivicay PD indication, GSK reinforces that strategic positioning, adding another pillar to its defense against generic erosion in older products and contributing to the overall narrative that its pipeline and lifecycle management efforts are delivering tangible results.
Representative product: the HIV treatment Tivicay PD
Among GSK’s many medicines, Tivicay PD stands out as a representative product for the company’s current strategy, because it embodies both scientific innovation and a focus on high-need patient populations. The formulation is designed specifically for children, using dispersible tablets that can be dissolved in water to aid administration for patients who cannot reliably swallow standard tablets, thereby improving adherence and enabling more precise dosing.
Tivicay PD works as an integrase strand transfer inhibitor, a class of antiretroviral therapies that block a key step in the HIV replication process, helping to reduce viral load to undetectable levels when used as part of combination therapy. By targeting the integrase enzyme, Tivicay PD can contribute to durable viral suppression, which is essential for preventing disease progression and reducing the risk of transmission, particularly crucial for children whose immune systems are still developing.
For GSK, Tivicay PD also exemplifies how targeted product design can differentiate offerings in a competitive therapeutic area. The pediatric formulation allows the company to address regulatory and clinical expectations around dosing flexibility and safety for young patients, potentially supporting preferential positioning in treatment guidelines and reimbursement decisions. The late August 2026 US approval for expanded use effectively broadens the addressable market for Tivicay PD and strengthens the business case for continued investment in pediatric and adolescent HIV research, including long-acting injectable regimens that could further ease treatment burdens for families.
GSK stock and investor takeaway
GSK stock trades on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker GSK, with late August 2026 quotes clustering in the low-to-mid $50 range and a documented close at $51.43 on August 26, 2026, followed by a pre-market indication of $51.28 on August 27, 2026. For investors, the key tension is between the stability suggested by this trading band and the potential upside or downside tied to forthcoming data, legal outcomes, and further regulatory decisions across vaccines, HIV, and specialty medicines.

Traditional & Complementary Medicine.url_match_title: Kebbi: Nasir Idris and forest reserve for traditional medicine - Head Topics
Traditional & Complementary Medicine.content:
Sometimes, a matter that is very much on one’s mind might just pop out of the blue to one’s pleasant surprise. I experienced this recently when the
Sometimes, a matter that is very much on one’s mind might just pop out of the blue to one’s pleasant surprise. I experienced this recently when the governor of Kebbi State, Nasir Idris, gave a directive to his Ministry of Environment.
Officials are to identify a forest reserve in Kalgo Local Government Area for cultivating and preserving indigenous medicinal plants. Idris gave this instruction when he received the leaders of the Coalition of the National Association of Nigerian Traditional Medicine Practitioners, Kebbi State chapter. It’s obvious the governor doesn’t belittle what’s indigenous to us as some do, a phenomenon I’ve commented on several times here.
According to Idris, he took the step he did because “We do not want our traditional medicine to vanish. ” As it turns out, his state hosts a large network of over 40,000 traditional medicine practitioners. I wonder if medical doctors in western medicine have that number in Nigeria, let alone Kebbi State. For me, the number reflects the importance of herbal medicine in community healthcare in this northwestern state.
And it’s neither a new or unsual phenomenon. Many of us know that our people use roots and herbs at a rate no official record has fully captured. This makes me wonder why we call our own traditional medical practice alternative medicine. In many communities, traditional medicine is the orthodox medicine.
I once noted on this page how, in the 1930s , British colonial officers in the northwest were celebrating that locals had begun to cautiously approach newly constructed Western clinics. Today, many locals still trust and depend on native medicine more than Western variants. For this reason, the need to preserve medicinal plants is something that’s always on my mind, considering the rate our forests are being depleted.
I like nature, I like forests, and I have a huge appreciation of the gifts of nature that are hidden in them. I grew up in a federal research institute with the serenity of nature all around me. Aside from rare timber, the next item of concern to me is the medicinal plants that are being lost at an alarming rate with the depletion of forests.
Some of these rare plants found only in the tropics are not only health, but they’re also wealth. As such, one doesn’t need to be a plant scientist or traditional medical practitioner to recognise the danger deforestation constitutes. All that one needs to see are the constant posts online of plants that are so common that we overlook, but those who know say such plants have properties that can cure so many ailments.
As a nature enthusiast, such information is of interest to me. More than this, I’ve paid attention to information that tells how some entities in Western nations dedicate themselves to preserving plants that have medicinal properties. Some of them are private organisations doing their best to assist mankind in preserving these gifts of nature. Some foreign scientists come to the African continent to collect these plants, which they take to their countries for preservation purposes.
This observation makes me wonder when Nigerian governments and scientists will do something similar. Now Kebbi State governor provides an answer. He does so at a time when large-scale destruction of the natural habitats of medicinal plants continues without any care on the part of everyone who should have it as their official task.
I suppose when these plants are wiped out, then one day we turn to foreign nations, asking them to donate to us samples of the plants they took from us in the first place. It’s the pattern in most matters, and this should be of concern to all of us. Must we always depend on foreigners for the safekeeping of what belongs to us? It’s a question political leaders need to ask and take a decision about.
A political leader doesn’t need to be a scientist to take the step Governor Idris did. All it takes is for one to have an awareness of natural medicinal properties as well as economic benefits packed into plants. Nations such as China and India have a medical ecosystem that benefits from this awareness. Both nations are leading examples of how traditional medicine has been part of general medical practice for decades.
Many natural items taken from the African continent go to those nations where traditional medical practice has become some sort of medical tourism. People from Western nations travel to China and India to receive traditional treatments for issues that defy Western medicine. Across the world, naturally derived drugs account for the majority of drugs approved since 1981.
To buttress the importance of medicinal plants, majority of the population in underdeveloped parts of the world, especially Africa, still relies on herbal medicine, mostly of plant origin or a combination of plants. As researches have established, this is attributable to the efficacy, affordability and perceived safety of these plants.
In an academic work by Babangida Abubakar and others, it’s demonstrated that different studies on medicinal plants continuously provide a platform for the potential discovery of novel compounds from uninvestigated and scarcely investigated plants. Such discoveries will be impossible if these plants are lost. The authors also note that in Nigeria, plants and herbal medicine continue to play a critical role as an alternative and affordable healthcare option for various diseases such as cancer, microbial infections, and diabetes, among others.
They state further that Kebbi State in particular has a rich repository of medicinal plants. In the entire northwestern Nigeria where Kebbi State is located, according to Abubakar and others, the majority of residents still heavily rely on traditional medicines from plants which have proven to be effective.
In addition, Kebbi State is very rich in traditional healing knowledge. Local studies in the state document well over 130 distinct plant species used to treat various viral infections, malaria, and other ailments. On their own, local traditional medicine practitioners have tried to preserve these vital botanical resources. Now, the state governor has stepped forward in a big way.
His effort will help traditional medical practice, and it’s a worthy cause considering that in Western nations both government and private institutions are involved in the conservation and preservation of medicinal plants. In fact, governments out there take such preservation as a national priority, and they allocate resources to facilitate the process. Out there, medicinal plants and their properties are preserved through a combination of legal habitat protection, controlled cultivation, high-tech germplasm storage, and scientific documentation.
These nations use structured bio-conservation frameworks to prevent the extinction of valuable flora. Government environmental agencies establish national parks, nature reserves, and protected public lands where native medicinal herbs grow in their natural ecosystems. There are strict regional regulations and permit systems which control the collection of vulnerable wild species such as Arnica or American ginseng, thereby preventing over-collection. Public and university-run gardens maintain living collections of rare and useful therapeutic plants for research and public education.
Facilities store dried seeds at very low temperatures or freeze plant tissues in liquid nitrogen to preserve the genetic blueprints of endangered medicinal species indefinitely. Laboratories use plant tissue culture and cloning techniques to rapidly multiply disease-free medicinal plants which ensures that the plants’ wild populations are not depleted.
Moreover, physically pressed plant specimens are stored in climate-controlled museum archives, while digital phytochemical databases map out plant DNA, chemical traits, and traditional uses. Official medical registries document standardised preparation methods and quality controls for plant-derived medicines to keep historical and clinical knowledge intact. There are also large libraries of pressed and dried plant specimens used by scientists to record global biodiversity and accurately classify plant species.
Specific institutions involved in such endeavours include The Chelsea Garden in London, UK, founded in 1673, which features dedicated pharmaceutical and world-medicine garden beds. The Padua Botanical Garden in Italy was established in 1545, originally built to cultivate medicinal simples. And there’s the United Plant Savers Botanical Sanctuary in Ohio, United States, which focuses explicitly on conserving native, at-risk medicinal woodland plants. When will Africa, and Nigeria in particular, enter this race to preserve nature’s gifts?
Of all the work of conservation happening in Nigeria, the one on medicinal plants is done the least. Governor Idris’ initiative is the first I hear of coming from any government. Private bodies need to be involved in this worthy endeavour for now and for the unborn generation. But such public-spirited effort that doesn’t present immediate gains and publicity hardly catches the interest of many in our nation.
The pattern needs to change, and here Governor Idris has set the ball rolling. I call on him to give this initiative the needed legal backing so that it continues into the future. Also, I urge him to take keen interest in the execution of the directive he gave. By seeing this through, he’ll have left a mark that many Nigerians will continue to appreciate him for.

Hanoi (VNA)
– Medical tourism is emerging as a high-value service sector, with many countries successfully building national brands and attracting large numbers of international visitors each year. Their experience offers useful lessons for Vietnam as demand for healthcare combined with medical treatment, rehabilitation, wellness and leisure continues to grow globally.
Strong potential
Health-related activities combined with tourism have existed in Vietnam for years, but modern medical tourism has developed mainly over the past decade alongside advances in healthcare and tourism.
Reports estimate that around 300,000 international visitors use medical services in Vietnam annually, generating 1-2 billion USD in spending on treatment, accommodation, transport and food.
Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City, Hue and Khanh Hoa are developing medical tourism products based on specialised healthcare services, leading doctors and professors, traditional medicine and wellness tourism.
International patients, mainly overseas Vietnamese and visitors from Cambodia, Laos, the Republic of Korea, Japan, Australia and Europe, seek services including dentistry, assisted reproduction, cosmetic surgery, health check-ups and high-tech treatment.
Meanwhile, Vietnamese people spend an estimated 2-3 billion USD each year on medical treatment abroad, highlighting the need to improve service quality and competitiveness.
Experts said Vietnam has strong advantages for developing medical tourism, including competitive healthcare costs, qualified medical professionals, rich natural and cultural resources, traditional medicine and a stable and secure environment.
With modern medical equipment, visitors can receive comprehensive examinations and get their results on the same day, without worrying about spending too much time on medical check-ups and treatment at healthcare facilities in Da Nang city (Photo: VNA)
The country has around 100 specialised medical facilities, including 13 hospitals meeting Joint Commission International (JCI) standards. Many hospitals have mastered advanced techniques such as robotic surgery, organ transplantation, cardiovascular intervention, cancer treatment and assisted reproduction.
Traditional medicine, including acupuncture, acupressure, massage and herbal therapies, is also gaining international recognition and could form distinctive medical tourism products.
Clear framework needed
The global medical tourism market is estimated at around 100 billion USD and forecast to grow 8-16% annually through 2035, with the Asia-Pacific region expected to expand faster than the global average.
To tap this potential, the Ministry of Health is coordinating with relevant ministries and sectors to develop a project on medical tourism development for 2026-2030, aiming to make Vietnam a competitive destination in Southeast Asia and gradually join Asia's leading group.
The project targets at least 20 hospitals meeting international quality standards and 30 standardised medical tourism packages by 2030. It also envisages a multilingual national medical tourism portal and database, as well as a national “Vietnam Medical Tourism” brand.
Vietnam aims to welcome around 750,000 international medical tourists by 2030, generating about 1 billion USD in direct revenue from medical treatment and healthcare services and 2.5 billion USD in total spending by visitors and accompanying persons.
Several localities, including Hanoi, Da Nang and Lam Dong, have begun developing their own medical tourism plans.
Hanoi is preparing a project for 2026-2030 with a vision to 2045 and promoting the brand “Hanoi – Vietnam's high-quality healthcare centre”, according to Dr. Nguyen Dinh Hung, Deputy Director of the Hanoi Department of Health.
Assoc. Prof., Dr. Tran Cao Binh, Director of the National Hospital of Odonto-Stomatology, said dentistry could become a pioneering field in Vietnam's medical tourism if quality and safety are placed at the centre. He called for a national dental tourism brand and network, with priority given to dental implants, full-mouth rehabilitation, cosmetic and digital dentistry, and orthodontics.
Prof. Dr. Do Tat Cuong, Chairman of the Vinmec Clinical Advisory Council, recommended stronger international communications, a multilingual national information platform, medical tourism visas for patients and relatives, and integrated transport, accommodation and sightseeing services.
Dr. Ha Anh Duc, Director of the Ministry of Health's Department of Medical Service Administration, said localities and healthcare providers should identify priority fields to guide investment. Traditional medicine and rehabilitation could be among Vietnam's distinctive products, given the country's medicinal resources and non-pharmaceutical therapies.
He added that relevant agencies are developing a set of standards for hospitals, clinics, and medical facilities participating in the medical tourism network, along with establishing a pricing mechanism for medical services and promoting Vietnam as a trusted destination for treatment, healthcare, rehabilitation, cosmetic services, and traditional medicine./.

Positioning Vietnam on the international
medical
tourism map.
Medical tourism is becoming a high value-added service industry
worldwide
, driven by the growing demand for combined medical examination, treatment, rehabilitation, healthcare, and relaxation. Many countries have successfully built national brands in this field, transforming their medical capabilities into a new competitive advantage for the tourism and service sectors.
The global medical
tourism
market is growing rapidly, opening up significant opportunities for countries with competitive healthcare, service, and tourism capabilities.
In Vietnam, healthcare-tourism activities have existed for many years, but the modern medical tourism model has only developed strongly in the last decade or so, alongside the modernization of the healthcare system and the upgrading of tourism service quality.
It is estimated that Vietnam receives approximately 300,000 international medical visitors annually, with total spending ranging from 1 to 2 billion USD, including medical examination and treatment costs, accommodation, travel, food, and related services.
Hanoi
, Ho Chi Minh City, Hue, Khanh Hoa, and several other localities are gradually developing medical tourism products based on their strengths in specialized hospitals, leading experts, wellness, and traditional medicine.
Ho Chi Minh City currently leads the country, accounting for approximately 40% of international visitors using medical services, thanks to its developed specialized healthcare system and dynamic tourism promotion efforts. Hanoi ranks second, while
Da Nang
, Hue, and Khanh Hoa are gradually developing medical tourism products based on their strengths in relaxation and traditional medicine.
However, the current clientele is still mainly concentrated among overseas Vietnamese and visitors from Cambodia, Laos,
South Korea
, Japan, Australia, and some European countries, using services such as cosmetic dentistry, reproductive assistance, aesthetics, general health check-ups, and some high-tech specialties.
Meanwhile, Vietnamese people still spend approximately 2-3 billion USD annually on medical examinations and treatment abroad, exceeding the total revenue from medical tourism to Vietnam. This shows that there is still significant potential to retain domestic patients and attract international visitors.
Our country also has many favorable conditions for developing this sector, from abundant tourism resources, numerous internationally recognized natural and cultural heritage sites, competitive healthcare service costs, highly qualified medical personnel, to a long-standing tradition of traditional medicine. A stable socio-political environment and a high level of safety also create additional advantages in terms of destination competitiveness.
In terms of expertise, Vietnam currently has approximately 100 specialized medical facilities, including 13 hospitals that meet JCI standards, mainly concentrated in Hanoi, Hue, and Ho Chi Minh City.
Many hospitals have mastered complex techniques such as robotic surgery, organ transplantation, cardiovascular intervention, cancer treatment, assisted reproduction, and specialized techniques in ophthalmology, otolaryngology, and dentistry. Alongside modern medicine, traditional medical methods such as acupuncture, acupressure, massage, and herbal remedies can also be developed into health care products combined with relaxation, creating a unique aspect for medical tourism in Vietnam.
In the field of dentistry, Associate Professor Dr. Tran Cao Binh, Director of the Central Dental Hospital in Hanoi, believes that quality and safety must be the foundation, and international patients should be at the center of the service design process. Development must meet international standards but be suitable for Vietnamese conditions, aiming to build a national dental tourism ecosystem with a focus on quality, safety, value, and experience.
You may also like
With the formation of the Vietnam Dental Tourism Network, competitive products such as dental implants, full-arch prosthetics, cosmetic dentistry, digital dentistry, and orthodontics have been identified as potential leading areas, creating a unique appeal for international visitors.
According to Professor, Doctor, and People's Physician Do Tat Cuong, Chairman of the Clinical Advisory Board of the Vinmec Healthcare System, developing medical tourism requires the synchronized participation of many ministries, sectors, and localities. International communication needs to be implemented in an integrated manner of healthcare, tourism, and culture, accompanied by a multilingual information platform, appropriate visa policies for patients and their relatives, and a system of support services from transportation and accommodation to sightseeing and relaxation.
From the perspective of healthcare facilities, the requirements include developing clear and transparent service packages with clear costs, ensuring high-quality specialized expertise, developing multidisciplinary capabilities, and being subject to strict quality and patient safety oversight. Only when international patients have access to comprehensive information about treatment facilities, doctors, techniques, costs, and support services can the competitiveness of Vietnam's medical tourism be sustainably enhanced.
Dr. Ha Anh Duc, Director of the Department of Medical Examination and Treatment Management, Ministry of Health, and the unit in charge of developing the "Medical Tourism Development Project for the period 2026-2030," believes that each locality and unit needs to clearly identify key areas to focus investment on. In particular, traditional medicine and rehabilitation are considered to have unique advantages due to their medicinal resources, non-drug treatment methods, and the ability to combine them with relaxation, meeting the needs of many international groups, especially those from Western countries.
Relevant agencies are currently studying the development of standards for hospitals, clinics, and medical facilities participating in the medical tourism network, while also refining the pricing mechanism and the method of connection between hospitals, tourism businesses, accommodation establishments, and supporting service providers.
Building an ecosystem to position Vietnam's medical tourism industry.
The global medical tourism market is currently estimated to be worth around $100 billion and could grow by 8-16% annually until 2035, with the Asia-Pacific region projected to grow faster than the overall average.
The large market potential requires Vietnam not only to exploit existing advantages but also to build clear policies, appropriate legal frameworks, standardize service quality, and create a brand that is competitive enough in the region.
The Ministry of Health is coordinating with other ministries and agencies to develop the "Medical Tourism Development Plan for the period 2026-2030," aiming to make Vietnam one of the most competitive medical tourism destinations in Southeast Asia, gradually rising to the leading group in Asia, with a synchronized service ecosystem ranging from modern medicine, traditional medicine, rehabilitation to comprehensive healthcare according to international standards.
The project is planned to be implemented in two phases, 2026-2028 and 2029-2030, aiming to have at least 20 hospitals meeting international quality standards, 30 standardized and operational medical tourism product packages, and the development of a multilingual national medical tourism portal and a national medical tourism database. A unified brand identity for "Vietnam Medical Tourism" is also expected to be issued and implemented.
By 2030, Vietnam aims to welcome approximately 750,000 international medical tourists, generating direct revenue of around US$1 billion from medical examinations, treatments, and healthcare, with total spending by tourists and their companions reaching approximately US$2.5 billion. These targets demonstrate that medical tourism is no longer viewed as a standalone supplementary product but is being positioned as a service segment capable of making a significant contribution to healthcare, tourism, and the economy as a whole.
In many localities, the development of medical tourism products is also being promoted based on their unique advantages. Hanoi is developing a plan for the development of medical tourism in the capital city for the period 2026-2030, with a vision to 2045. Dr. Nguyen Dinh Hung, Deputy Director of the Hanoi Department of Health, said that Hanoi is gradually building and promoting the brand "Hanoi - Vietnam's high-quality medical center," aiming to become a leading healthcare and medical tourism destination in Southeast Asia.
In its plan for developing medical tourism in Ho Chi Minh City for the period 2025-2030, with a vision to 2045, the city aims to become a competitive medical center in the region, based on its advantages in professional capacity, quality of treatment, reasonable costs, and a hospital system that is increasingly applying technology and standardizing care procedures according to international standards.
You may also like
Beyond attracting patients with advanced techniques, the long-term goal is to create an ecosystem that connects medical examination, treatment, healthcare, rehabilitation, and relaxation, thereby generating high-value-added medical tourism products with competitiveness in the international market.
Associate Professor Dr. Tang Chi Thuong, Director of the Ho Chi Minh City Department of Health, said that the city is promoting the development of a specialized healthcare network, strengthening connections between public, private, and international hospitals to leverage the strengths of each unit, improve treatment quality, and create a foundation to attract domestic and international patients. The city's healthcare capacity is being demonstrated through many complex techniques and cases of foreigners proactively choosing Vietnam for treatment.
Specifically, according to the leaders of the Ho Chi Minh City Department of Health, medical tourism is unlikely to gain momentum if healthcare facilities, tourism businesses, and service providers continue to develop independently. Collaboration with travel agencies plays a crucial role in bringing international and domestic tourists closer to medical services, while also connecting treatment with accommodation, transportation, relaxation, and destination experiences.
Accordingly, instead of individual products, Ho Chi Minh City will form a complete ecosystem in which hospitals, travel agencies, hotels, resorts, and supporting services all participate in a unified value chain.
Therefore, the three elements of building a core product, developing an ecosystem, and positioning a brand need to be implemented simultaneously. When the expertise of healthcare is transformed into distinctive products, connected to the tourism ecosystem, and promoted by a sufficiently strong brand, Ho Chi Minh City can turn its existing advantages into genuine competitiveness, moving towards becoming a leading medical tourism destination in the region.
With approximately 300,000 international medical visitors using medical services annually, Vietnam already has an initial market. However, to transform from a cost-effective destination into a leading medical tourism brand in Southeast Asia, the "low price" advantage alone is not enough.
The draft plan for the development of medical tourism in the period 2026-2030 therefore aims to establish a unified national policy framework, improve institutions, develop products, services and brands, gradually transform medical tourism into a high-value-added interdisciplinary service sector, and position Vietnam as a reputable destination in the region.
The goal by 2030 is to make Vietnam one of the most competitive medical tourism destinations in Southeast Asia, gradually rising to the leading group in Asia; while simultaneously building and positioning the national brand of medical tourism in the international market.
